line: Up to four players walk through waves of monsters on one screen, picking weapon upgrades that fire on their own, and try to last until the thirty-minute bell.
You wander a nature sanctuary together photographing birds and filling in a shared guidebook; nothing in it attacks you.
Each of you plays a potato holding up to six weapons, surviving timed waves of aliens and shopping for upgrades between them.
A 64-player top-down battle royale with cartoon animals, where your squad drops in together and loots, drives and shoots its way to the last circle.
Two players each get a portal gun and test chambers that need all four portals to solve, in a campaign separate from the solo story.
A hand-animated roguelite where a pair hunts bosses that flee between rooms, swapping weapons and powerups as you chase them.
Up to six snack characters throw boomerangs in small arenas, and team rounds let you gang up on the bots or on each other.
Four survivors fight through zombie campaigns where the director decides when the horde hits, and nobody can wander off alone.
You dig, build and fight bosses together in a 2D world, pooling resources toward gear nobody could craft alone.
Two players evolve one pathogen together, choosing transmissions and symptoms, and race to infect the world before a cure lands.
Two bounty hunters shoot their way through pixel-art gang hideouts in couch co-op, taking cover and trading boss fights.
Four climbers scale a mountain that changes every day, sharing food and rope and hauling each other up when someone slips.
You deliver packages through chaotic platforming levels together and can build and publish your own courses for the group.
A physics sandbox with no goals: you spawn props and ragdolls on shared servers and play the game modes the community built.
You and up to three sheepdogs herd colorful flocks across levels, splitting the flock between you to reach the pens.
A roguelite platformer with destructible terrain where you dig down through the Abyss together and share whatever loot comes up.
Two possums raid a town for food while guards chase you, and the run ends when you have eaten enough or been caught.
The 1996 shooter with its expansions, which you can play through in co-op with up to three others on the same server.
Four survivors push through the original zombie campaigns, with the AI director timing the hordes to whoever lags behind.
A physics fishing game for up to four players: you crash on an island and have to catch, cook and boat your way home.
A calm card game about birds for up to five players, each building a chain of bird effects on their own board over four rounds.
The whole open-world campaign can be played as a pair, with one of you driving while the other leans out of the window shooting.
Four players share one tower defense map, each placing monkey towers and spending their own money as the bloons speed up.
A side-scrolling brawler where up to four band members fight through a punk-rock apocalypse and level up their characters.
An action RPG where up to six players clear randomized dungeons together, with pets that run back to town to sell your loot.
A military simulator with large co-op missions, where a squad plans and carries out operations across open terrain on dedicated servers.
An open-world shooter about speed, with a hoverboard and a grappling hook, playable in co-op from the first mission.
Four to fifteen crewmates do small tasks on a ship while impostors pick them off, and everyone argues in meetings about who did it.
An open-world platformer where up to four round heroes smash through themed levels and collect everything in sight.
You build and run a waterpark together, designing slides and watching ragdoll guests fly off them while someone else handles the staff.
A fast 2D action platformer with a two-player campaign built on long combos and a lot of gore.
Up to four action-movie heroes run and gun through destructible levels, and every rescued prisoner swaps you to a new bro with a new gun.
A digital board game for four where you roll, fight and collect stars with cute characters, and cards ruin everyone's plans.
A tower defense where two players place monkey towers along the same track and split the money each round.
Up to six players brawl through a pixel-art beat 'em up as the turtles, April, Splinter and Casey, with team moves and shared pizza.
A hand-drawn beat 'em up where up to four of you walk through the city punching gangs, with the old games' characters unlockable.
You hunt spiders through suburban houses with whatever weapons you find, burning most of the furniture in the process.
You film each other doing dangerous things in a monster-filled facility and upload the tape; scarier footage gets more views.
Four vault hunters shoot and loot across Pandora in one shared campaign, with enemies and guns scaling to the party.
A rogue-lite physics brawler where you and a friend throw office workers through windows on the way up the corporate ladder, picking new moves between floors.
You cook and serve in one restaurant, then rebuild the kitchen layout between days as the orders get harder.
Two to four cooks shout orders across kitchens that split apart, catch fire and drift while you try to plate dishes in time.
You share a wilderness where food, sanity and daylight all run out, and splitting the chores is how you make it through winter.
You start on a raft with a hook, pull junk from the sea together, and build it into a floating base while a shark circles.
Wobbly ragdoll characters stack, drag and climb each other through physics puzzles, and most of the fun is falling off.
Escape rooms built for up to ten players where you pass clues around and solve the locks together.
Each player adds one trap or platform to the level, then everyone runs it, so the course gets nastier every round.
A first-person dungeon crawl where each of you plays a different class and permadeath means the survivors carry on alone.
Four heroes run a roguelite shooter with different weapon builds each time, reviving each other between rooms.
A free two-player puzzle game: you are split up in a frozen castle and can only talk through walkie-talkies to describe what you see.
A free online action game where a squad of four runs missions together, with a long campaign and frequent updates.
The whole WW2 campaign can be played by two players, spotting targets for each other and timing shots across large maps.
Up to four players run one farm, splitting the planting, mining and fishing, and sharing the money.
Twelve players putt through the same mini golf course at once, with power-ups that let you knock each other off the hole.
